# RealityCheck

RealityCheck is a local-first HTML note checker plus an evidence-first Web quality audit skill and CLI. The zero-install note checker reads selected HTML files only inside the user's browser and checks encoding, document structure, broken attachments, internal navigation, machine-specific paths, remote dependencies, executable scripts, mobile readability, accessibility, and unfinished AI placeholders. It can download JSON evidence, copy bilingual repair tasks, and generate a new conservatively repaired copy without overwriting the source. In an authorized Codex Skill task, `--prepare-repair` creates a bounded working copy with local assets so Codex can repair it directly, rerun the same check, and return before/after reports without asking the user to paste a report prompt back into Codex.

For professional Web QA, RealityCheck can preview a bilingual audit plan before browser access. It then uses a real installed Chrome, Edge, or Chromium browser to stress responsive layouts, user journeys, API and network recovery, links, publishing metadata, visual baselines, performance, accessibility, security policy, and aggregate Cookie/Web Storage privacy budgets. It writes bilingual human reports plus machine-readable JSON, SARIF, JUnit, repair plans, policy reviews, issue drafts, manifests, verification evidence, and freshness-aware GO/REVIEW/NO-GO release decisions.

RealityCheck never treats an unsupported check as passed. Audit mode is read-only, remote targets require explicit authorization, and generated GitHub issue drafts are local files that are never submitted automatically.

## Quick start

Open the zero-install checker and choose an HTML file or note folder. For the CLI, clone the repository, run `npm install`, then run `npm run note -- ./my-notes`. Add `--fix-safe` for only the three conservative metadata repairs, or let the `$realitycheck` Skill use `--prepare-repair` for a complete agentic working copy without modifying the originals. To preview an existing Web project policy without browser access, run `npm run realitycheck -- plan --config realitycheck.config.json`. To audit an authorized local app, run `npm run audit -- http://localhost:3000`.
